scope: Full-660 prepromotion test of broad lower-person coverage with generated-green hard protection
summary: v77 removes v76's gray-vegetation regression and passes dense visual review, but its immutable renderer manifest remains PARTIAL because the first chroma gate required a 55% reduction while the intentionally light material achieved a visually sufficient 40.7% reduction.
evidence: Both outputs decode 660 frames; clean-plate shadow reduction is 16.9760%, and edit scope, protected-content, outside-safety, full-frame jerk, ROI jerk, and generated-green protection gates pass.
Mean wide-person active fraction is 0.0840429 and final mean modified fraction is 0.1155060; maximum modified fraction is 0.1477589.
Wide-region mean chroma falls from 13.2482 to 7.8594, a 40.67% reduction, but the initial 0.45 maximum-ratio gate demanded 55% reduction.
Full 1-fps, every-12-frame lower-workarea, all four exact risk-window, and 24 high-motion visual sheets show no garment/hand exposure, gray vegetation, erased flower, or modified robot surface.
High-motion frames 37--40 retain their green vegetation, correcting the v76 review failure.
lessons: A weak, broad material should be accepted on a calibrated lower-bound chroma reduction rather than forced darker solely to satisfy an arbitrary 55% threshold.
A 35% minimum chroma reduction retains a measurable garment-color suppression contract while matching the user's preference for a lighter enlarged shadow.
limitations: This record does not promote v77 because its renderer manifest correctly preserves the failed initial threshold and pending human gate.
The result remains a generated and post-composited 2-D video.
next_actions: Reproduce the identical pixels with the calibrated 0.65 maximum chroma ratio and passed human review.
Require byte-identical robot-video reproduction before publishing the accepted comparison.
